title: Union Budget 2026-27: Sitharaman's Ninth Consecutive Budget
shortDescription: FM Nirmala Sitharaman presented a 'Yuva Shakti-driven' Budget on 1 February 2026, with a 4.3% fiscal deficit target, record defence allocation, and 'Semiconductor Mission 2.0'.
genZNote: Three Kartavyas, one Budget — growth, capacity, and Sabka Sath Sabka Vikas. If an MCQ says 'Kartavya', it's this Budget.

sections.heading: What Happened
sections.body: Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman presented the Union Budget 2026-27 in the Lok Sabha on 1 February 2026 — her ninth consecutive Union Budget. She described it as a "Yuva Shakti-driven" Budget guided by three self-described Kartavyas (duties): accelerating economic growth, building people's capacity, and ensuring Sabka Sath, Sabka Vikas (inclusive access to opportunity).

sections.heading: Key Facts
bullets: Fiscal deficit target for FY 2026-27: 4.3% of GDP.
Non-debt receipts estimated at ₹36.5 lakh crore; total expenditure at ₹53.5 lakh crore; capital expenditure ₹12.2 lakh crore.
Defence sector given an all-time-high allocation of ₹7.85 lakh crore.
'Semiconductor Mission 2.0' announced, alongside dedicated Rare Earth Corridors for mining, processing, and manufacturing.
'Biopharma Shakti' strategy proposed to position India as a global biomanufacturing hub.
Real GDP growth for 2025-26 estimated at 7.4% (Economic Survey 2026, presented 29 January 2026); nominal growth for 2026-27 projected around 8-10%.

sections.heading: Why It Matters
sections.body: The Union Budget is one of the highest-yield current-affairs topics every year — numbers like the fiscal deficit target, defence allocation, and named new schemes ('Semiconductor Mission 2.0', 'Biopharma Shakti') are classic one-line MCQ fodder, and this Budget also directly links to Gujarat's semiconductor push.

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: Union Budget 2026-27, presented 1 February 2026 by FM Nirmala Sitharaman (her 9th consecutive Budget), targeted a 4.3% fiscal deficit and announced Semiconductor Mission 2.0.
keyFacts: Presented 1 Feb 2026; 9th consecutive Budget by Sitharaman.
New: Semiconductor Mission 2.0, Rare Earth Corridors, Biopharma Shakti.
commonConfusion: The Economic Survey (29 Jan 2026) and the Budget (1 Feb 2026) are two separate, back-to-back documents — don't merge their dates.

highYieldFacts: Fiscal deficit 4.3% of GDP; capex ₹12.2 lakh crore; defence ₹7.85 lakh crore.
Semiconductor Mission 2.0 and Rare Earth Corridors are the flagship new-scheme names to remember.
commonTraps: Mixing up the Economic Survey's date (29 Jan) with the Budget's date (1 Feb).
mustRemember: 9th consecutive Budget by Nirmala Sitharaman, presented 1 February 2026.
